title: Willard Robison's Deep River Orchestra and William Grant Still
summary: He describes Robison's spiritual-based music and recalls William Grant Still as one of Whiteman's staff arrangers.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: It wasn't anything that I should -- I'm very happy to mention it because it happened. But now, to get to another guy that I had experience with that you might like to hear was Willard Robeson. Did you ever hear of Willard?
Well, I know about him, you know, something about him. I know some of this music.
Yeah. Well now, Willard was quite a

character and also an excellent talent. He had a -- what he called a Deep River Orchestra. And he used to delve into these spiritual books, and he dug out any number of them. I don't know where he got them, but they were always -- they had blues in, and they had a lot of colored -- Black people's works in them, you know.
Well anyway, I ran into Willard. He called me, wanted to get together on something. I think we were doing a show together with Shilkret. And --
But you had known him long before this?
Well, I didn't know him when he was in the Whiteman band.
But I had heard about him. But we came in contact with each other, and he wanted to do some things together, with his Deep River Orchestra.
Now, Billy Still, William Grant Still, he was one of the arrangers in the Whiteman band. He, Ferde and I were three, you know, we were the arranging staff at one time.
I guess he was one of the leading Black composers of that period.
Well, I guess he was. I had heard of
him through the Deep River Orchestra. They had done a lot of wonderful stuff there.

Now, I used to listen to that over WOR when they first -- when the station first started out to play the -- they used to do a lot of work there. And most of that was Bill Still's work. And I guess he -- I know we needed help on the Old Gold Show, and Whiteman got him to help out. He did his two a week like Ferde and I.
So I didn't see him after that. I have an idea he must have gone to the Coast when the situation turned up. Maybe, you know, when Whiteman cut the band down, I think he got out at that time.
